estimand: Bidirectional causal transmission elasticity between prediction market prices and media attention
assignment_narrative: Exogenous regime shifts in volatility generated by discrete presidential debates, assassination attempts, candidate withdrawals, and regulatory rulings
interpretation_boundary: Semi-elasticity of public/media attention per unit probability change across US battleground swing states during the 2024 campaign

diagnostics.finding: Volatility regimes are determined by dated political shocks (debates, assassination attempt, candidate switch) exogenous to daily platform noise.
Balanced daily panel across 7 key swing states over 250 trading days with full price and attention support.
Standard errors account for spatial autocorrelation and cross-sectional dependence via Driscoll-Kraay and Conley spatial HAC.
Substantial within-state odds movement (SD = 0.0657, range 0.396 to 0.729) provides identifying variation after controlling for state fixed effects.
Rigobon heteroskedasticity identification conditions verified: residual variance ratio across regimes Δσ_v² / Δσ_u² > 0 with invariant structural parameters.
Local projections trace impulse response trajectory over horizons h=0 to 5 days, showing peak narrative impact at t+4 and 6-day half-life.
Driscoll-Kraay Newey-West Bartlett kernel with L=4 days and Wild Cluster Bootstrap p-values prevent false precision from serial correlation.
